A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLIP-ICM under the same title. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot and linear-probe classification results, ablations, domain-prompt experiments and ImageNet-C robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification results across five DomainBed datasets, together with augmentation, hyperparameter and domain-prompt analyses.

M1.justification: The projection objective and SVD procedure in Algorithm 1 are retained. However, v1 Equation (7) uses projected dot-product softmax scores, whereas v2 Equation (3) and Section 4 explicitly use normalized cosine similarity. The PDFs do not establish whether normalization changes inference or makes a previously implicit step explicit.

E1.justification: v2 removes the supplementary ImageNet-C corruption and clean-ImageNet evaluation from v1 Appendix G. VLCS, PACS, Office-Home, TerraIncognita, DomainNet and the domain-prompt scenarios remain; PACS and Office-Home are moved to Appendix H.

E2.justification: The ImageNet-C comparison against the ResNet-50 baseline and CLIP Linear-probe disappears. Comparator membership in the retained DomainBed, SIG, DPL and domain-prompt comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Removing the ImageNet-C experiment also removes its mCE and clean-error evaluation protocol. Retained experiments preserve the leave-one-domain-out design, backbones, dataset splitting procedure, seven augmentations and stated linear-probe training budget and regularization.

E4.justification: v1's ImageNet-C robustness analysis and illustrative zero-shot examples in Figure 1 are removed. The augmentation-combination, lambda, invariant-dimension and domain-prompt analyses remain; combining the three ablation plots in v2 Figure 5 does not add experiments.

E5.justification: Retained tables preserve their uncertainty values, and both versions describe random-seed-dependent splits without specifying repeated-run counts. v2 explains that some cited results lack source-reported error bars, but introduces no new uncertainty estimates, statistical tests or estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All eleven retained result tables preserve their numerical values after matching relocations. v1 Table 7 disappears, including mCE values of 76.7%, 62.92% and 51.74% for the ResNet-50 baseline, CLIP Linear-probe and CLIP-ICM Linear-probe, respectively, and their clean-error results. The illustrative predictions in v1 Figure 1 also disappear.

T1.justification: v2 revises the causal graphs and replaces v1's transportability formulation with a conditional-prediction decomposition. It changes the formal risk from negative log-likelihood to classification error and replaces the Rademacher/Massart argument with an H-delta-H divergence analysis and conditional Theorem 3.3. Proposition 4.1 also introduces a text-cardinality condition and substantially revises the identifiability proof. The intervention-identification theorem is largely retained.

C1.justification: The central theoretical contribution is reframed. v1 emphasizes conditions for capturing transportable causal mechanisms and a lower OOD generalization bound; v2 emphasizes conditional risk superiority depending on empirical risk, complexity and domain divergence. Its abstract also newly claims insignificant computational overhead.

C2.justification: v1 explains failure primarily through unobserved latent factors and non-transportability. v2 develops an explanation involving unknown target-domain variant factors, changing decision boundaries and the need for low invariant-predictor training error. It connects these requirements to the projection objective and adds an explicit classification-only evaluation limitation.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix G newly specifies a single NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and average training duration below one hour per result. It also states that code accompanies supplementary material, although availability cannot be verified from these PDFs. Existing pseudocode, augmentation choices and classifier settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ben-David et al. (2010), Chuang et al. (2020) and Yang et al. (2023), and a dedicated comparison with IRM in Appendix J.1. Several citations disappear, including Daunhawer et al. (2023) and Hendrycks and Dietterich (2019). The broader causal-representation and OOD positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, problem formulation and causal narrative are extensively rewritten. Theory and methodology become separate sections, while causal background, implementation details and ablations are reorganized into appendices. v2 also adds a notation guide and a more complete appendix roadmap.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 redraws the causal graphs, adds a decision-boundary illustration and two notation tables, removes the introductory prediction examples and separate selection-diagram illustration, and relocates benchmark tables. Three ablation figures become one composite, with corrections to conflicting zero-shot/linear-probe captions.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition, qualifies the main risk claim and adds useful implementation disclosures, but removes v1's corruption-robustness evidence. The central theoretical revision does not establish improved validity: Appendix D infers actual risk ordering by subtracting upper bounds in Equations (28) and (30), retaining a problem present in v1's Appendix E. These clarity gains, evidence losses and unresolved theoretical support prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
